title: Medal of Honor Act
official_title: To amend title 38, United States Code, to increase the rate of the special pension payable to Medal of Honor recipients, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Enacted as Public Law 119-43 on December 1, 2025. Sponsored by Rep. Troy Nehls (R-TX) with 4 cosponsors; per the printed legislative history, it passed the House on February 26, 2025 and the Senate on November 7, 2025 before being signed.
summary: Raises the VA's special monthly pension for Medal of Honor recipients by replacing the fixed $1,406.73 rate with a rate tied to the veterans' disability-compensation schedule. It also extends through January 31, 2033 the rule capping VA pension at $90 a month for certain veterans in Medicaid-funded nursing homes.
brief: Replaces the fixed Medal of Honor special pension of $1,406.73 a month with a higher schedule-based rate, and extends the Medicaid nursing-home pension cap of $90 a month through January 31, 2033.

top_lines.headline: Medal of Honor Pension Increase
subs: Fixed rate of $1,406.73 replaced with a schedule-based rate
New rate tied to compensation for a veteran without dependents
No double increases in the same year

top_lines.headline: Pension Cap Extension
subs: Cap of $90 a month for Medicaid nursing-home veterans extended
Cap now expires January 31, 2033 instead of November 30, 2031

items.main: Names the Act the "Medal of Honor Act" and sets out findings on the Medal of Honor and the special pension paid to those on the Medal of Honor Roll.
items.detail: The findings state that Medal of Honor recipients have earned a substantial and historic increase to the special pension paid monthly under section 1562 of title 38.

sections.label: Section 3 — Increase in Department of Veterans Affairs Special Pension Payable to Medal of Honor Recipients

items.main: Replaces the fixed special pension of $1,406.73 a month for Medal of Honor recipients with a rate equal to the monthly compensation paid to a veteran without dependents under section 1114(m) of title 38, increased to the next intermediate rate under section 1114(p).
items.detail: The special pension is paid by the VA to each living person whose name is on the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Coast Guard Medal of Honor Roll, with surviving spouses also eligible under existing law. Tying the rate to the compensation schedule replaces the prior fixed dollar amount.

items.main: Bars the pension's annual cost-of-living adjustment in any year when the amount was already otherwise increased that year.
items.detail: Existing law raises the special pension every December 1 by the same percentage as the Social Security benefit increase. The new rule prevents that adjustment from stacking on top of another increase in the same year.

sections.label: Section 4 — Extension of Certain Limits on Payments of Pension

items.main: Extends from November 30, 2031 to January 31, 2033 the expiration of the rule capping VA pension at $90 per month for certain veterans receiving Medicaid-covered nursing-facility care.
items.detail: Under that rule, a veteran with no spouse or child who is covered by a Medicaid plan for nursing-facility services cannot be paid more than $90 a month in VA pension after the month of admission; the same limit applies to surviving spouses with no child. The extension lengthens the cap's life by 14 months.

underreported.section: Section 4 — Extension of Certain Limits on Payments of Pension
underreported.summary: Extends by 14 months, through January 31, 2033, the $90-per-month VA pension cap for veterans with no spouse or child receiving Medicaid-covered nursing-facility care, and for surviving spouses with no child.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill's title and findings concern honoring Medal of Honor recipients; this provision extends a limit on pension payments to a different group of veterans entirely.

underreported.summary: The Secretary may not apply the annual December cost-of-living increase to the special pension in a year when the amount was otherwise increased.
underreported.why_unreported: The section is labeled as a pension increase; this clause withholds the routine annual adjustment in any year another increase occurs.

gaps: The bill pegs the new pension to the section 1114 rate schedule but states no dollar figure, leaving the actual amount to the compensation tables in effect at any given time.
The findings call for a substantial and historic increase, but the bill does not state the size of the increase in dollars.
The bill extends the Medicaid nursing-home pension cap to January 31, 2033 without stating any criteria for whether the cap should continue past that date.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Nehls
featured_quotes.text: First and foremost, it has been a sincere pleasure to work with the chairman and his staff to advance this important legislation to the House floor. It is an honor to stand with him today. I also extend my gratitude and thanks to my colleague, Mr. Pappas, for co-leading this bipartisan legislation with me for the last two Congresses. Mr. Speaker, today, I rise in strong support of H.R. 695, the Medal of Honor Act. The Medal of Honor is our Nation's highest and most prestigious military decoration that can be awarded.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Cruz
featured_quotes.text: Since 1863, Presidents of the United States have awarded the Medal of Honor to more than 3,500 of the bravest men and women ever to wear the uniform of this Nation. Each one has demonstrated valor, gallantry, and heroism above and beyond the call of duty, with acts so selfless, so extraordinary that they stand as beacons of courage for future generations. In 1960, Congress passed Public Law 6556, establishing the Army and Navy Medal of Honor Roll and entitling each Medal of Honor recipient to a modest special pension of $10 per month for life.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Pappas
featured_quotes.text: The Medal of Honor is our Nation's highest military decoration. It recognizes the extraordinary valor that distinguished men and women of our military demonstrated in critical moments during their service to our great Nation. There are 63 living Medal of Honor recipients, including heroes like Army Staff Sergeant Ryan Pitts of New Hampshire, who served two tours in Afghanistan. During his second deployment, hundreds of insurgents attacked the Army base where he was stationed.

added: Rule barring the annual cost-of-living adjustment to the Medal of Honor special pension in any year the amount was otherwise increased
modified: Medal of Honor special pension — fixed monthly rate of $1,406.73 replaced by the section 1114(m) compensation rate for a veteran without dependents, increased to the next intermediate rate under section 1114(p)
Medicaid nursing-facility pension cap — expiration extended from November 30, 2031 to January 31, 2033

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended
